newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Global One sees good business propects in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Global One sees good business propects in Asia.

text.p: Telecommunications consortium Global One said on Tuesday it saw bright business propects in Asia in the next few years as deregulation became more entrenched in the region.

The company, an alliance of France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint, has not been able to sell many of its voice-based products in the region yet due to tight controls, but it was optimistic this would change.

"The way we market is by the regulation in each country. We can't sell a lot of voice products in many countries because they won't be deregulated until 1998," Asia Pacific president Richard Kalbrener told reporters.
"There's of course the World Trade Organisation asking all countries to deregulate. In 1998, a lot of them will," he said.
Kalbrener also said Global One, along with 13 others, had been given a Virtual Private Network licence from Hong Kong's Office of Telecommunications Authority.
The licence allows Global One to provide its customers with a closed telecommunications network for transmission of voice, facsimile and data to their offices and arms overseas.
Global One has 18 offices in Asia including Australia, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, New Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.
